observador.title: Alentejo 2030 abre concurso de 5,8 milhões de euros
observador.description: A CCDR do Alentejo explicou que o aviso agora lançado tem candidaturas abertas por fases, sendo que a primeira delas termina no dia 30 deste mês e a última a 31 de maio de 2027.

observador.title: A guerra entrou numa nova fase para a Ucrânia? — Debate
observador.description: Após ataques ucranianos em São Petersburgo e uma carta aberta de Zelensky a Putin, cresce a ideia de uma viragem no conflito. Estará a Ucrânia a ganhar vantagem sobre Putin?

observador.title: Putin já tomou conhecimento da proposta de Kiev
observador.description: O porta-voz russo, Dmitri Peskov, afirmou que Putin "já foi informado" da carta aberta de Zelensky, que propõe o encontro entre os dois presidentes. Mediação europeia já foi rejeitada por Putin.

observador.title: Urso "inteligente" atacou quatro pessoas no Japão e fugiu
observador.description: Vítimas têm idades compreendidas entre os 20 e os 80 anos. Acredita-se que urso tenha escapado de fábrica onde foi encurralado, ao abrir uma janela. Escolas locais chegaram mesmo a ser encerradas.

observador.title: Quatro mortos em queda de avioneta na Península da Ístria
observador.description: Avioneta, de matrícula alemã, terá entrado em espiral antes de se despenhar na Península da Ístria. As vítimas são de nacionalidade austríaca e as autoridades croatas estão a investigar acidente.

observador.title: Proteger o ambiente sem comprometer o acesso a medicamentos
observador.description: A propósito do Dia Mundial do Ambiente, a Europa enfrenta o desafio de conciliar a sustentabilidade ambiental com o acesso contínuo a medicamentos essenciais.

observador.title: 12h. Greve dos não docentes. 60% das escolas encerradas
observador.description: São números do Sindicato Nacional dos Trabalhadores dos Serviços e de Entidades com Fins Públicos. Ainda, o Grupo Vita vai levar ao Vaticano as preocupações sobre os casos de abuso sexual arquivados.

observador.title: GNR apela à prevenção de práticas lesivas para o ambiente
observador.description: No Dia Mundial do Ambiente, a GNR relembra que "a proteção ambiental é uma responsabilidade partilhada" e apela à prevenção e denúncia de práticas lesivas. 20.535 autos foram efetuados em 2025.

observador.title: Aniversário da repressão de Tiananmen levou a sete detenções
observador.description: Hong Kong assinalou o 37º aniversário da repressão que levou à morte de dez mil pessoas, em 1989, na Praça de Tiananmen. Cinco homens e duas mulheres foram detidos temporariamente.

observador.title: FIFA proíbe entrada de  garrafas reutilizáveis no Mundial
observador.description: O organismo máximo do futebol mundial afirmou na quinta-feira que a decisão de proibir as garrafas, que poderiam ser atiradas, visava "prevenir riscos e lesões para jogadores e espetadores".

observador.title: Luísa Sobral edita novo álbum em outubro
observador.description: De acordo com o agenciamento de Luísa Sobral, o oitavo álbum da artista, que é editado em 9 de outubro, "assinala a sua aproximação à música tradicional portuguesa".

observador.title: Cuba. ONU alerta para deterioração de condições humanitárias
observador.description: Entre sanções impostas pelos EUA e desastres naturais constantes, a crise energética em Cuba agrava-se: "Todos os serviços básicos estão a ser afetados pela falta de combustível", afirmou o OCHA.

observador.title: Portugal não precisa apenas de boas empresas
observador.description: Portugal tem empresas industriais competentes, exportadoras e inovadoras. Falta, em demasiados casos, transformá-las em empresas com escala para influenciar mercados, atrair talento e criar mais valor

observador.title: ONU pede mais de 600 milhões de dólares para o Líbano
observador.description: As deslocações constantes da população civil, a capacidade insuficiente de acomodação e as perspetivas limitadas de regresso seguro estão a agravar a vulnerabilidade dos cidadãos, declarou a ONU.

spiegel.title: Eishockey: Harold Kreis muss als Bundestrainer gehen
spiegel.description: Wenn in knapp elf Monaten die Eishockeyweltmeisterschaft in Deutschland startet, wird Harold Kreis nicht mehr an der Bande stehen. Drei unbefriedigende Turniere in Folge waren dem DEB zu viel.

spiegel.title: Madonna gibt zum Pride Month Überraschungskonzert am Times Square in New York
spiegel.description: Zum Auftakt des Pride-Monats lud Madonna über die Dating-App Grindr zum Gratisauftritt auf dem New Yorker Times Square. Die 67-jährige »Queen of Pop« präsentierte Songs aus ihrem kommenden Album »Confessions II«.

spiegel.title: Taiwan: Mehr als 84 Meter hoch – Forscher stoßen auf Rekordbaum
spiegel.description: Neun Jahre haben Wissenschaftler nach ihm gesucht, dann standen sie in einer abgelegenen Region Taiwans vor einem außergewöhnlichen Zypressengewächs.

spiegel.title: Winsen an der Luhe: Polizei nimmt nach Bedrohungslage an Schule Tatverdächtigen fest
spiegel.description: In einem Gymnasium in Winsen an der Luhe soll am Morgen ein Bedrohungsanruf eingegangen sein. Die Polizei evakuierte die Schule. Ein Tatverdächtiger ist bereits ermittelt.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Frankfurt Flughafen: Lufthansa-Dreamliner nach Panne abgeschleppt
spiegel.description: Plötzlich fiel die Boeing auf die Nase: Nach dem alarmierenden Unfall des Dreamliners am Frankfurter Flughafen wurde die Maschine in der Nacht enttankt, angehoben und ins Technikgelände verbracht. Die Flugsicherung ermittelt.

spiegel.title: Endlich Gleichbehandlung? Sharon Stone und Keke Palmer haben da ein paar Ideen
spiegel.description: Gleiche Rechte für Männer und Frauen? Zwischen den US-Schauspielerinnen Sharon Stone, 68, und Keke Palmer, 32, liegt ein großer Altersunterschied, aber beim Gespräch über dieses Thema waren sie im Flow: »Als Erstes nehmen wir euch das Viagra weg«.

spiegel.title: Uno-Sicherheitsrat: Deutschland plant angeblich erneute Bewerbung ab 2035
spiegel.description: Nach der gescheiterten Abstimmung um einen Sitz im Sicherheitsrat der Uno will Deutschland sich nach Angaben der Agentur Reuters erneut bewerben, für zwei Perioden ab 2035.

spiegel.title: Aue-Bad Schlema: Freie Sachsen bezwingen AfD – gewinnen sie nun auch die OB-Wahl?
spiegel.description: Stefan Hartung ist Neonazi, Mitglied der »Freien Sachsen« und in Aue-Bad Schlema beliebt. Nun könnte er Oberbürgermeister der Stadt werden. Sogar die AfD überlässt ihm das Feld.

spiegel.title: Eurozone: Wirtschaft schrumpft im ersten Quartal überraschend
spiegel.description: Neue Daten zeigen, dass die Wirtschaft im Euroraum im ersten Quartal leicht geschrumpft ist. Vor allem Irland hat seine Daten nach unten korrigiert, auch wegen Trumps Zöllen.

spiegel.title: Nastassja Kinski reagiert auf Debatte über Nacktszene in Wim Wenders' »Falsche Bewegung«
spiegel.description: »Es war nicht leicht, aber seit Langem fällig«: Nastassja Kinski hat sich zum Streit über Wim Wenders’ »Falsche Bewegung« geäußert. Die Schauspielerin fordert einen Umschnitt, der Regisseur zog seinen Film vorerst zurück.

spiegel.title: Deutschland hat bislang 52.000 Opfer des NS-Regimes oder ihre Nachkommen eingebürgert
spiegel.description: Opfer des Hitler-Regimes und deren Nachkommen können in Deutschland über ein erleichtertes Verfahren eingebürgert werden. Viele haben davon schon Gebrauch gemacht, fast genauso viele warten auf die Einbürgerung.

spiegel.title: Norwegen: Kronprinzessin Mette-Marit auf Warteliste für Lungentransplantation
spiegel.description: Die norwegische Kronprinzessin hat seit Jahren mit einer unheilbaren Lungenkrankheit zu kämpfen. Einem Arzt zufolge macht nun ihr Gesundheitszustand eine Transplantation erforderlich – so bald wie möglich.

spiegel.title: NBA-Finals: Liga sperrt Flitzer lebenslang
spiegel.description: Im NBA-Spiel zwischen den San Antonio Spurs und den New York Knicks war ein Mann auf das Spielfeld gestürmt, offenbar um ein Foto zu machen. Die Aktion hat nun Folgen, auch für eine zweite Person.

spiegel.title: Hannover: Feuerwehrmann stirbt nach Wettkampf »FireFit European Championships«
spiegel.description: Auf der Rettungsmesse Interschutz in Hannover hat sich ein tragisches Unglück ereignet: Ein Feuerwehrmann brach bei einem Wettbewerb zusammen und starb anschließend im Krankenhaus.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Wie reagiert Wladimir Putin nach Brief von Wolodymyr Selenskyj?
spiegel.description: Der ukrainische Präsident hat direkte Gespräche mit seinem russischen Kriegsgegner vorgeschlagen, auf neutralem Boden. US-Präsident Trump reagiert wohlwollend. Beim Wirtschaftsforum in Sankt Petersburg ist nun Putin am Zug.

spiegel.title: James Handy ist tot: Schauspieler mit Stichwunde im Vorgarten gefunden
spiegel.description: Er hatte eine jahrzehntelange Karriere in Film und Fernsehen, spielte in Krimiserien und einen Barkeeper in »Top Gun: Maverick«. Nun wurde James Handy in seinem Vorgarten erstochen, ein Verdächtiger wurde festgenommen.

spiegel.title: Australien: Behörden stellen illegal gehaltene Kakerlaken im Wert von 120.000 Euro sicher
spiegel.description: Es soll der bislang größte Fund illegal gehaltener Wirbelloser in der Geschichte des Landes sein: In Australien sind Kakerlaken im Wert von rund 120.000 Euro sichergestellt worden.

nyt.title: Vanilla Ice Is In, Bret Michaels Is Out: Trump’s Battle for Celebrity Validation
nyt.description: President Trump has pursued fame his entire adult life. Now in his second term in the White House, he is finding how little power he has to force cultural figures to fall in line.

nyt.description: The agency had warned it could run out of money within months, but its regulators said suspending payments to a retirement fund had given officials more time to find a permanent solution.

nyt.description: James Murdoch says acquiring New York magazine and Vox has nothing to do with his father. But in some ways, it’s a tribute.

npr.description: A coastal development project linked to Jared Kushner is facing resistance in Albania. The government says the project will transform the nation, but environmental campaigners and critics oppose it.

The multidisciplinary team is a unique blend of professional tree climbers, ecologists, geologists, and remote sensing specialists.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. But a defense buildup on this scale would jeopardize economic growth and regional unity, and could lead Southeast Asian countries to gravitate toward China’s strategic orbit.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s AI Vision and Its Limits
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI is clear-eyed about the limits of techno-utopianism. But its vision of technology directed toward human flourishing needs to be extended to include the interests of every sentient being, human and nonhuman, biological or—possibly—artificial.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Is Fueling a Global Debt Shock
proj-syn.description: Once again, a global crisis is disproportionately burdening countries that did not cause it. Across the Global South, the food- and energy-price shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East has morphed into a debt shock that demands an urgent international response.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Incentives for Climate Action
proj-syn.description: As the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global oil and gas flows, countries are increasingly focusing on short-term energy priorities to the detriment of long-term decarbonization goals. In such a context, the difficult task of designing climate policies that realign incentives takes on new importance.

proj-syn.title: The US and India Have Become Regional Rivals
proj-syn.description: While the US views India as a counterweight to China in Asia, it balks at the idea of Indian regional dominance, preferring a pluralistic order.
